board.name: Delaware Board of Medical Licensure and Discipline, with the Regulatory Council for Physician Associates (Division of Professional Regulation)

ce.categoryRules: 100 hours CME per 2 year cycle, of which 50 hours Category 1
ce.nccpaNote: Current NCCPA certification is deemed to meet the 100 hour requirement; holding it is not itself a renewal condition (it can be imposed on re-entry licences).

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substance prescribing practices, chronic pain treatment, or other topics related to prescribing controlled substances
topicMandates.appliesTo: holders of a Delaware controlled substance registration (CSR)

topicMandates.topic: Delaware Office of Controlled Substances mandatory course (safe prescribing, pain treatment, opioid use disorder)
topicMandates.appliesTo: practitioners applying for a Delaware CSR (attested on the CSR application per DPR); regulation 3.1.2 requires completion within the first year of obtaining registration; not CE and not countable toward the 2 hours

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours every 2 years for CSR holders (attested at CSR renewal); one-time 1 hour two part DPR course attested on the CSR application (regulation: within the first year of registration)
ce.firstRenewalProration: First renewal: licensed under 1 year, no CME; licensed 1 to 2 years, 50 hours (DPR CE page)
ce.boardPageConflict: The DPR PA CE page says "50 hours of Category I and 50 hours of Category 2" and dates the cycle "April 1 and March 31 even-numbered years"; regulation 13.2.2 requires 50 Category 1 within 100 (rest unrestricted) and the DPR renewal page and licence expiry are March 31 of odd years. Use the regulation.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written collaborative agreement created by the PA and physician team or facility, kept on file at the PA's primary practice location and produced to the Board or Council on request; not filed with the Board. No renewal interval set in statute.
practice.notes: HB 325 (85 Del. Laws c. 253, signed May 12, 2026) lets PAs with more than 6,000 postgraduate clinical practice hours apply to the Regulatory Council for independent practice authority. It is implemented on the earlier of May 12, 2027 or Board approval of the Council's enabling regulations, so as of 2026-10 a collaborative agreement is still required unless those regulations have been approved. A collaborating physician may collaborate with no more than 4 PAs at a time.

prescribing.prescriptiveAuthorityNote: PA prescriptive authority and practice authority are subject to biennial renewal with the Regulatory Council (renews with the licence; no separate registration identified).
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 2 hours controlled substance related CE every 2 years for CSR holders

board.name: Delaware Board of Nursing (Division of Professional Regulation)

rn.renewalDeadline: February 28, May 31 or September 30 of odd-numbered years (depends on original issue date; new licences September 30)
rn.practiceHoursForRenewal: 1,000 hours in past 5 years or 400 hours in past 2 years

aprn.title: APRN (role designation C.N.P. for nurse practitioners)
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: separate APRN licence; requires a Delaware RN licence or a compact multistate RN privilege
aprn.renewalDeadline: Same date as the Delaware RN licence; September 30 of odd years if no Delaware RN licence
aprn.ceNote: No APRN-specific CE hours in regulation for renewal; the APRN must meet the national certifying agency's recertification requirements and the RN CE (30 hours if Delaware RN). Practice hours: 1,500 in 5 years or 600 in 2 years in the role and population focus.
aprn.aprnCompact: Delaware enacted the APRN Compact (24 Del.C. ch. 19B) but the chapter is marked effective only upon fulfillment of the contingency in 83 Del. Laws c. 110 s. 2; not operational for tracking.

unverified: Whether the Board has approved the Regulatory Council's enabling regulations for PA independent practice authority (HB 325) before 2026-10: the current 1700 regulation loaded has no independent practice provisions, so the latest implementation date is May 12, 2027.
The 1700 regulation still uses "supervising physician" in PA prescriptive authority (13.3.1.1, 13.3.1.2) while the statute uses collaboration; the statute controls.

No APRN specific CE or pharmacology hour requirement for renewal exists in 24 DE Admin Code 1900-8.12 (only national recertification and 1,500/600 practice hours); pharmacotherapeutics hours apply only to reinstatement after 2 or more years out of practice (8.12.7.2, 8.12.7.3).
sourceNote: regulations.delaware.gov is a script rendered site; regulation text was loaded through the site's own API (POST https://regulations.delaware.gov/api/AdminCode/regulation, regulationUrl=/AdminCode/title24/<n>) which returns the current codified HTML.
corrections: DE PA and APRN: corrected the CSR mandatory 1 hour course timing. Regulation 3.1.2 says new registrants complete it within the first year of registration; DPR asks for an attestation on the CSR application. It is not CE.
DE PA and APRN: confirmed the Delaware CSR expires June 30 of odd-numbered years (DPR CSR renewal page), resolving the researcher's open item.
DE PA: added the first renewal proration (under 1 year licensed: none; 1 to 2 years: 50 hours) from the DPR CE page.
DE PA: flagged that the DPR CE page misstates the split (50 Cat 1 + 50 Cat 2) and the cycle years (even); regulation 13.2.2 (50 of 100 Category 1) and the odd-year March 31 expiry control.
DE RN: added the first biennium exemption for exam licensees (9.2.6.1) and that an NP's national certification or recertification earned in the biennium counts as 20 of the 30 RN hours (9.3.3).
DE RN: the 1 hour abuse topic now cites the regulation and spells out its scope (sexual/physical abuse, exploitation, trafficking, domestic violence, child abuse reporting).
DE APRN: added that Delaware enacted the APRN Compact (ch. 19B) but it is contingent and not in effect; no multistate APRN licence to track.
DE PA: added primary cites for the 4 PA collaboration cap (1700-13.1.1.7.2) and the 6,000 hour floor (1772(e)); confirmed HB 325 s.23 implementation clause and that HB 325 made no CE change.
